Take opposite edges \(AB\) and \(CD\), and let their midpoints be \(M\) and \(N\).

Unfold faces \(ABC\) and \(ACD\) into the plane along \(AC\). Place
\[
A=(0,0),\quad B=(1,0),\quad C=\left(\tfrac12,\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\right),\quad D=\left(-\tfrac12,\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\right).
\]
Then
\[
M=\left(\tfrac12,0\right),\qquad N=\left(0,\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\right).
\]
So this unfolded straight path has length
\[
\sqrt{\left(\tfrac12\right)^2+\left(\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)^2}=1.
\]
This segment crosses \(AC\) at its midpoint, so it is a valid surface path.

In any unfolding, images of \(M\) and \(N\) in the triangular lattice differ by a vector whose horizontal component is at least \(\tfrac12\) and vertical component at least \(\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\), so no path can be shorter than \(1\).

\[
\boxed{1}
\]
